title: Resolve and persist notification icon hints and desktop identity
head: eb274743cfda
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A missing or stale file-backed image-path is persisted as a working icon even when the copy fails
leads.consequence: When image-path is nonempty but missing, over 5 MiB, or disappears before the queued copy (including a sender-owned /tmp file), it shadows an installed desktop icon, persistablePopup rewrites appIcon to file://.../images/<stem>-appIcon, copyImagesScript removes the temp and continues, and the JSON still records the nonexistent target. While live, the card takes Quickshell's image hint first; on restore a bare-path hint's image:// source has been dropped (and a file:// hint's copied image can fail likewise), while appIcon points at a nonexistent copied file instead of the available desktop icon. No later reconciliation repairs the JSON. The same sequence can affect DND-silenced history. Validate a copy before committing its URI or retain a usable icon fallback.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus D3; published (failed image copy)

leads.summary: Desktop icon fallback cannot use AppLibrary's live icon index for newly installed applications
leads.consequence: An app/web-app installed while the shell is running can publish a new DesktopEntry and Icon= under ~/.local/share/icons, but Qt's themed icon cache can miss the new name. AppLibrary explicitly maintains a refreshed file index so the menu shows it; the notification's snapshot keeps only the icon name and its card calls Quickshell.iconPath(name,true), bypassing that index. Its icon slot remains empty (or glyph-only) for an app whose icon the menu already displays, until Qt's themed-icon cache refreshes (typically a shell restart). Pass the indexed path/resolver to the card or resolve a file path when snapshotting, including the index update path.
leads.triage: unconfirmed runtime claim on pre-existing card path; dropped

leads.summary: The name/startup-class fallback excludes valid NoDisplay desktop entries
leads.consequence: For a sender with app_name only, blank app_icon and no desktop-entry hint, an installed application marked NoDisplay=true still has a desktop entry and Icon= but is absent from DesktopEntries.applications.values, so both the snapshot lookup and card fallback silently return no icon. Quickshell can look that entry up by ID, but only if the sender supplies desktop-entry (not this case). If the feature is intended for all installed apps, include an ID lookup where available or document this limitation.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus E NoDisplay note; report only

leads.summary: A bad image-path hint still creates Quickshell's magenta missing-texture image, hiding the new app-icon fallback
leads.consequence: On a non-file image-path (e.g. themed icon misspelled), Quickshell v0.3.1 emits nonempty image://icon/<name> regardless of whether QIcon can resolve it. The card's image.length branch bypasses iconSource(appIcon), so even a correct appIcon from an installed desktop entry cannot displace the upstream provider's magenta placeholder. After persistence image:// drops, and appIcon is the misspelled hint, yielding an empty icon instead of the available desktop icon. This rendering problem existed on the base for bad image-path, but the new 'image-path then desktop entry' fallback does not repair it and now persists the bad hint.

leads.summary: Related PR #13312 reserves snapshotOf's new third argument for an exec-token, colliding with this PR's desktop entries
leads.consequence: The two open, nonstacked PRs both alter snapshotOf(notification,timestamp,third) and replacementSnapshot(notification,id,timestamp,fourth), one passing a desktop entry list and one a security token. The three-way merge contains 4 conflict markers in NotificationLogic.js and 6 in Service.qml. Selecting one side loses icon matching or rejects first-party --exec tokens; passing a list where the token is expected also makes the token comparison meaningless, so the security gate and icon lookup need separate parameters. Requires separate arguments, reordered callers, and tests for both icon matching and token rejection after merge.

leads.summary: Related PR #7545's per-application delivery identity collides with both snapshot fields and the replacement argument
leads.consequence: #7545's snapshot adds sourceKey/source/desktopEntry for delivery modes; its fourth replacementSnapshot argument is the prior identity, while this PR's fourth argument is the desktop entry list. The three-way merge has 4 NotificationLogic.js and 2 Service.qml conflict markers. Keeping only this PR's snapshot branch loses per-app sourceKey/origin, so configured 'off' or 'history' web-app modes may route by the wrong browser/alias; keeping #7545's snapshot discards this PR's icon persistence. Reconcile both fields and use separate args for identity and desktop entries before either lands.
leads.triage: factual, in opus/merge-conflicts.txt (#7545); not listed publicly for brevity

leads.summary: Related PR #12567's web-app icon override conflicts with the new card fallback and its exact shape assertion
leads.consequence: #12567 adds a webappIconSource between per-notification image and browser app icon. Its card hunk and this PR's card hunk conflict. Accepting only this PR's branch loses the browser web-app override; accepting #12567's branch loses the new desktop-entry fallback. Its regex assertion for a one-line smallIconSource at pr12567.diff:383-390 will also fail if the current multi-line card is retained. A merged card should select image, web-app icon, explicit/resolved app icon, then desktop-name fallback and update both tests.

leads.summary: Related PR #9985's image-path QML change and test fail to compose with the new card fallback
leads.consequence: #9985 expects image to go through iconSource and pins its former one-line ternary with a regex. git merge-file using #9985's own base produces a card conflict but its tests merge cleanly: selecting its card branch removes this PR's desktop-name fallback; selecting this PR's branch fails #9985's regex, even though Quickshell v0.3.1 already transforms non-file image-path into image://icon before the card. Reconcile the QML and update the test to check behavior rather than an old ternary shape.

leads.summary: The direct desktop-entry icon lookup duplicates Quickshell's existing byId lookup, while its fixture suppresses that upstream result
leads.consequence: For a real notification with blank app_icon and a valid desktop-entry ID already in Quickshell's catalog, Quickshell v0.3.1 resolves byId and fills notification.appIcon before the service snapshots it, including NoDisplay entries. The newly added appIconFor(desktopEntry) branch is therefore bypassed for the exact positive case the tests claim it fixes; the synthetic fixture supplies a populated desktopEntry but artificially empty appIcon. This does not invalidate the distinct app-name fallback, but the PR should distinguish the upstream direct-ID behavior from its new behavior, and test a case upstream cannot already resolve.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus E; published as Design note

leads.summary: New icon fallback tests still pass when the actual QML card ignores the desktop fallback
leads.consequence: The tests exercise appIconFor() and snapshotOf() as pure JS, but not that NotificationCard calls appIconFor(app, root.desktopEntries). Mutating the real card to return the empty string on that branch while keeping its JS helper and snapshot intact passes all 158 assertions. Thus an old persisted popup with empty appIcon, or a live card whose snapshot was resolved before an app became available, can lose the promised card fallback unnoticed. Add a QML binding-shape assertion or a real card rendering check, in addition to the existing model tests.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus C01; report only (predates eb274743)

limits: No native compositor was assigned, so image rendering and same-session Qt icon-cache behavior were checked by pinned Quickshell source and AppLibrary code, not a screenshot. Conditional image-provider behavior should be validated visually if a compositor becomes available.

Related PR merges were checked with git merge-file using each PR's own merge base, but conflict-bearing combinations were not executed until a human resolves the conflicts. GitHub's mergeable property describes merge against each PR's base, not cross-PR compatibility.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier follow-up](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12741#issuecomment-5803882925) and the [author's update](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12741#issuecomment-5832168798), checked at `eb274743`.

**Verified:** the new commit resolves `app` and `appIcon` when the notification arrives, so the icon now survives persistence and replay. The notification suite passes 158/158 (144 at `3e7f900c`). Three cases that had no icon after restore at `3e7f900c` keep it at `eb274743` (JavaScript probes modelled on Quickshell v0.3.1 source):

| Sender | `3e7f900c`, restored | `eb274743`, restored |
|---|---|---|
| `notify-send -i <themed name>` | no icon | themed name kept |
| `notify-send -i /abs/path.png` | no icon | persisted as a copy of the file |
| `desktop-entry=org.omarchy.agent`, `image-path=com.mitchellh.ghostty`, empty `app_name` | no icon, `app` empty | themed name kept, `app` = `org.omarchy.agent` |

Senders that set `app_icon` or per-notification image data keep their priority.

**Earlier notes at this head:**
- **Test coverage (still resolved):** the `appIconFor` fixtures are unchanged, and removing the startup-class, hyphenated, name or id match path, or case folding, each still fails an assertion.
- **libnotify comment (resolved):** `eb274743` removed the whole explanatory comment above `appIconFor`. The new four-line comment makes no libnotify claim.
- The earlier test-scope note that empty app names fall outside the fallback no longer applies to senders with a `desktop-entry` hint: `app` now falls back to it. Senders with no hint, image or matching entry stay iconless.

### Clicking a replayed toast now focuses a window by desktop-entry id

The description says there are no window-focus changes, but the new `app` fallback reaches click-to-focus. Restored and replayed rows never run a live "default" action, so a click falls back to `focusApp(entry)`, which returns early on an empty `app` and otherwise runs `omarchy-hyprland-focus-app <app>` (`Service.qml:374-410`). That helper takes the first window whose class matches the value as a case-insensitive regex.

```text
replayed agent toast, click
  3e7f900c: app = ""                  -> focusApp returns, no window focused
  eb274743: app = "org.omarchy.agent" -> first window with that class is focused
```

`bin/omarchy-agent:144` opens every agent window with `--app-id=org.omarchy.agent`. A sandboxed run of the unchanged helper with a mocked `hyprctl` listing two agent windows focused the first one. Live Ghostty toasts are not affected, because Ghostty registers a default action.

**Impact:** with more than one agent open, clicking a replayed agent toast can focus a different agent than the one that notified. Other desktop-entry-only senders now get click-to-focus by id where the click previously focused nothing.

**Suggested change:** either state this as intended in the description, or keep the desktop-entry id in its own snapshot field so `focusApp` keeps its previous input (#12884 adds a separate `desktopEntry` field).

**Optional test improvement:** each of these edits still passes all 158 assertions:
- dropping `desktopEntries` from `Service.qml`'s `snapshotOf` call, which turns off the desktop-entry and app-name icon lookups at receive time;
- dropping it from either `replacementSnapshot` call;
- removing `desktopEntryChanged`;
- moving the desktop-entry and app-name lookups ahead of `image-path`.

The test file already pins `Service.qml` wiring with regex assertions, so the calls can be pinned the same way. A fixture with both an `image-path` and a resolvable desktop entry would pin the order the description states.

**Failed image copy on restore:** a file-backed `image-path` is now stored in `appIcon`, and the persisted entry points at its copy whether or not the copy succeeds. If the copy fails (source gone, over the 5 MB limit or not a regular file), the restored card points at a missing copy and hides the desktop-entry fallback that `3e7f900c` showed for a named sender. The merge base showed no icon in that case either.

**Design note:** Quickshell v0.3.1 already fills `appIcon` from a `desktop-entry` hint that matches an installed entry id, and already maps a non-`file:` `image-path` into `image` as `image://icon/...`. The icons were lost because `persistablePopup` drops `image://` values. Persisting the name or path behind them would be an alternative that keeps per-notification image content out of `appIcon`. The current approach does fix the targeted senders.

**Related PRs:** #9985 and #12567 serve different purposes, but each conflicts with this PR on the same `smallIconSource` binding in `NotificationCard.qml`, and #12567 sets its own order (image, web-app icon, app icon). #9660, #12111 and #13312 each use the new third parameter of `snapshotOf` for something else.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** the notification suite ran at the merge base, `3e7f900c` and `eb274743` in an isolated sandbox, with labelled diagnostic mutations and JavaScript probes modelled on Quickshell v0.3.1 source. `omarchy-hyprland-focus-app` ran against a mocked `hyprctl`. Quickshell, GLib and Ghostty source were read directly. Merge conflicts were checked with `git merge-tree` against open PR heads. No live notifications, QML runtime or visual rendering, and the author's `./test/all` result was not reproduced.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
